> **The four-day week, revisited**
> 
> When a large trial of the four-day working week was completed, the headlines were enthusiastic: productivity had been maintained, and almost every participating company chose to continue. A closer look at the data suggests a more complicated picture.
> 
> The companies that volunteered were not typical. Most were small, and a majority were in knowledge industries where output is measured in projects rather than hours. Manufacturing and healthcare were barely represented. Critics argue that a scheme which works for a software firm of forty people may tell us little about a hospital.
> 
> There is also a question about what “maintained productivity” means. In most participating firms, the reduction in hours was accompanied by significant changes to working practices: shorter meetings, fewer internal emails, and stricter limits on interruptions. It is possible that these changes, rather than the shorter week itself, produced the results. Several researchers have pointed out that no company tested the reforms without also cutting hours, so the two effects cannot be separated.
> 
> None of this means the idea has failed. Employee wellbeing improved substantially and consistently, which is a result in itself. But the claim that any organisation can move to four days without cost goes considerably beyond what the evidence supports.

**Multiple choice (7–9):**

1. According to the passage, the companies in the trial were
   A. representative of the whole economy B. mostly small knowledge-based firms C. mainly hospitals and factories
1. The writer suggests that improved results may have been caused by
   A. shorter hours alone B. changes to working practices C. higher salaries
1. The writer’s overall attitude to the four-day week is
   A. strongly opposed B. entirely convinced C. cautiously positive

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 2, ≥250 từ: In many countries people are working longer hours than in the past. What are the causes and what can be done?
writing.bai_mau:
In a number of countries, the average working week has become longer rather than shorter, despite advances in technology. This essay will examine the main causes of this trend and suggest how it might be reversed.

Several factors appear to be responsible. The most obvious is economic pressure: as living costs, particularly housing, have risen faster than wages, many employees feel obliged to work overtime simply to maintain their standard of living. A second cause is technological. Because staff can now be contacted at any hour, the boundary between work and private life has become blurred, and many people continue answering messages long after leaving the office. Finally, in some workplaces long hours are treated as evidence of commitment, which creates pressure to stay late regardless of output.

Fortunately, a number of measures could improve the situation. Governments could enforce existing limits on working time more strictly, as several European countries have done. Employers, for their part, should assess performance by results rather than by hours spent at a desk; if promotion depended on output alone, the incentive to stay late would largely disappear. Trials of a four-day week have produced encouraging results, with productivity maintained or even improved.

Individuals also have a role. Setting clear limits, such as not checking email after a certain time, protects both health and long-term productivity.

In conclusion, longer working hours result mainly from financial pressure, constant connectivity and workplace culture. Addressing the problem will require action from governments, employers and employees together, since no single group can resolve it alone.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Đề hỏi hai phần (causes + solutions) và bài trả lời cả hai, mỗi phần một đoạn riêng. Ba nguyên nhân, ba nhóm giải pháp, kết luận tổng hợp cả hai.
Cấu trúc "causes → solutions" rõ ràng. Đánh số ý bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên: The most obvious is… A second cause is… Finally… thay vì Firstly/Secondly máy móc.
economic pressure · feel obliged to · standard of living · boundary… blurred · evidence of commitment · regardless of output · enforce limits · incentive · connectivity.

Bị động (can be contacted, be reversed) · điều kiện loại 2 (if promotion depended… would disappear) · mệnh đề nguyên nhân (Because staff can now be contacted…) · mệnh đề quan hệ (which creates pressure).

dang_hoc: Đề dạng causes + solutions thì bắt buộc chia hai phần. Chỉ viết nguyên nhân là mất nửa điểm Task Response.
Giải pháp nên chia theo chủ thể: chính phủ · doanh nghiệp · cá nhân. Dễ viết mà mạch lạc.
Tránh Firstly/Secondly/Thirdly cả bài. Thay bằng: The most obvious… A second cause… Finally…
Kết luận phải nhắc lại cả hai phần của đề, không chỉ một.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Chỉ trả lời nguyên nhân, quên giải pháp → mất điểm nặng nhất ở dạng đề này.
❌ Giải pháp chung chung ("people should work less") → phải cụ thể và khả thi.
❌ Dùng "Nowadays" mở bài → cực kỳ phổ biến và bị đánh giá là sáo rỗng.
❌ Lặp lại chính xác từ trong đề nhiều lần → phải paraphrase.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 1 — Work: What do you do? / Do you work long hours? / Would you like to change anything about your job?

cau_tra_loi.mau: I work in e-commerce for an electronics retailer. My role involves managing product content and increasingly automating data processes.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "My role involves…" là cách nói chuyên nghiệp hơn "I do…".

cau_tra_loi.mau: Not excessively, though it varies. Month-end is intense — sometimes ten or eleven hours — but the rest of the time it's fairly reasonable.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "Not excessively, though it varies" — trả lời có điều kiện, thể hiện chính xác chứ không tuyệt đối.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Would you like to change anything about your job?
cau_tra_loi.mau: I'd like fewer meetings, honestly. A lot of what gets discussed could be handled over email, which would free up time for actual work.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "which would free up time" — mệnh đề quan hệ với điều kiện, nâng điểm ngữ pháp.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời có sắc thái, không tuyệt đối, có mở rộng.
involves · automating · excessively · intense · free up time.
which would free up · could be handled (bị động + modal).

meo_noi: "Not excessively", "fairly reasonable", "it varies" — ngôn ngữ giảm nhẹ, dấu hiệu của band cao.
Đừng trả lời "yes, very long" rồi dừng. Luôn thêm điều kiện hoặc ngoại lệ.
